# Synthetic extraction fixtures

Generated locally on 2026-09-05 with reportlab (PDF), python-docx (DOCX),
python-pptx (PPTX), and openpyxl (XLSX). These contain invented test text,
never customer documents. The tests need only Go and the existing parser.

Expected facts: `Revenue is 123`, `Storage` / `35.50`, and Russian text
`Привет, команда` or `Выручка` in Office formats. The PDF has two pages.
These small examples check parsing and content retention, not OCR accuracy,
complex layout fidelity, or model answer quality.

## T13 authored acceptance corpus

`t13/manifest.json` freezes 20 source fixtures, their SHA-256 hashes, manually
written labels and acceptance criteria before corpus extraction runs.
`t13/generate.py` creates invented text, never reads parser or OCR output and
never derives its labels from a parser. The checked-in fixtures need only Go
and the existing parser for baseline tests; regeneration needs the listed
Python libraries, macOS Arial/Fred, and ffmpeg.

Document quality requires exact ordered Unicode letter/number tokens, ordered
paragraphs, all six table cells in row-major order, and exact labeled PDF/PPTX
page counts. Punctuation/whitespace are layout separators; plain Unicode TXT
also requires byte-exact preservation. The corpus includes EPUB/ODT, valid
empty TXT, malformed/empty/encrypted documents, and a scanned PDF with no
automatic OCR fallback. A deterministic large TXT is generated inside the test.
A successful empty scanned-PDF boundary is not an OCR quality result.

Run `go test -p 1 -ldflags=-w -count=1 ./pkg/extract ./pkg/chunker`.
For actual English OCR, run the same command with
`LEVARA_T13_TESSERACT=1`. This requires an installed Tesseract binary and
English trained data; it does not download a model. OCR uses whitespace-only
normalization, retains case/punctuation, reports CER/WER, requires CER <= 0.05,
WER <= 0.10, and exact source-authored numeric facts (17, 23, 40). Default runs
explicitly skip the OCR quality case. CLI diagnostic separation and unavailable
backend tests run without an installed engine.

The labeled 16 kHz mono PCM WAV was generated by installed local Fred TTS.
Whisper quality remains unmeasured: the test verifies an explicit unavailable
endpoint error, never substitutes a stub transcription for quality evidence.
The small clean corpus does not establish noisy-scan, complex-layout, Russian
OCR, real-speech, or production-distribution accuracy.
